trickyParts: kvwatch completeRead takes applyMu, rechecks generation/stopped/Check error/disconnect count under mu, sweeps with mu released, then sets following only if still valid; a read a disconnect overlapped completes nothing (extension of D2 to disconnects).
Marks are collected only between Begin (BeginRead) and End (after CompleteRead's sweep), so a following cache keeps no growing key set.
The session copy prunes age-expired rows only while Following(); Get still answers not-found for an expired retained row.
Session and interest Delete read the revision fence only when the read under way began in the handle's epoch (readEpoch), so an old bucket's revision never carries into the new one.

The web's react-query retry policy retries 5xx, so a refilling notice appears after retries are exhausted; rows of the last successful read stay on screen but no absence claim is made unless the latest read succeeded.
deviations: Race tests ran with zig as the C compiler and external linking (the pod image at this base has no gcc); all passed. CI is the canonical race lane.
Disconnect: a read overlapped by a disconnect completes nothing (plan named only Check for skipping the state write).
Reap's liveness is func(sessionID) (bool, error), shared by both reapers through sessionMayBeLive; roleHolderMayBeLive wraps it.
Added Disconnected/NeedsRead passthroughs on the three adapters and WithSessionClock on the session registry (test clock).
An unconfigured listener reads route_status_reason 'unreachable', so the reason is non-null exactly when route_status is unknown.
Unclaimed filter had no notice; one was added (data-testid unclaimed-unchecked). MentionComposer reads useAgents itself (ConversationTab never passed agents), so its states come from its own hook.
Simplify pass applied three changes (marks lifecycle, Marks.MarkCurrent, session Delete via applyEntryLocked); skipped findings are listed in the PR Thermo line.
Perf fix folded in under the standing rule: per-record pruneLastSeenLocked made a read cost entries x swept sessions (15.5 s vs 1.6 s at rig scale).
Forward-merged main once (GitHub CONFLICTING); fingerprint changed; all proofs re-run at b6d4733.

Round 2 detection is an in-process stream probe (STREAM.INFO per watcher every 2 s, 1.5/s per listener) plus a gate holding a post-read record on a confirmation older than 4 s, not JetStream advisories: the listener's NATS users have no subscribe permission on $JS.EVENT.> (packages/envoy/infra golden configs), so advisories would need a NATS auth rollout first. Check stays the fallback.

Known limit: if the gate's synchronous STREAM.INFO fails with an error other than stream-not-found, the record is applied with Following unchanged (a transient JetStream error must not force a full re-read).

Fixed under the standing rule: nats.go v1.50.0 KV watcher init timer can send on a closed channel when the subscription ends as the timer fires (still present upstream); kvwatch stops a replaced/discarded watcher only after its scan marker. Remaining exposure: nats.go's own unsubscribe and End at shutdown.

Ledger: the tester's red test subscription_end_test.go changed only in its handle construction (js.KeyValue -> bus.OpenKeyValue(conn, js, ...), and the bus.KeyValue{KeyValue: handle} literal -> handle): a legacy handle cannot yield its *nats.Conn (nats.go kv.go:539), so the literal cannot watch through the jetstream package. Its connection close, held record, timing sweep and rounds are unchanged. Architect informed beforehand.

Round 3 also moved History and Keys off the legacy API (ReadHistory, roleKeys via ScanExistingKeys), since both run the legacy watcher internally; the redelivery sweep's scan now refuses a stalled or early-ended scan instead of taking a partial one.

ReadStreamState reads through jetstream.JetStream.Stream (a fresh STREAM.INFO each time) rather than the jetstream KV handle's Status, which writes shared stream info with no lock (nats.go v1.50.0 jetstream/stream.go:460); the race detector caught it.
The watch's consumer create is bounded by nats.go's 5 s request wait for a deadline-free context (jsm.go:1791-1795), not a kvwatch create timer.
Round 2's deferred stop is removed: with no init timer a stop is safe at any time; a stopped watcher is still read until it closes.

Residual (nats.go, cannot be fixed from our side, no panic): jetstream WatchFiltered sets its closed handler after Subscribe returns, so a subscription ending in that window leaves the reader goroutine blocked; the new architect-requested test cannot run at 57e48f1 because it targets the new API, so the tester's red test is the negative control.
